To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the data mining approach to dynamically generating compound critiques is more efficient in terms of user interaction time and the multi-attribute utility approach is more efficient in supporting the user to find the best product.

(1) compound critiquing techniques are a promising way of supporting users to efficiently navigate complex product space, (2) users' preferences can be captured more efficiently using a multi-attribute utility approach than by a data mining approach, and (3) users are more satisfied when the interface strategy is to generate critiques from the most popular attributes.

the data mining-based approach is more effective in supporting users to navigate a complex product space, while the multi-attribute utility-based approach is more efficient and more effective in supporting user navigation in a simpler product space.

the data mining approach is more efficient in terms of the number of critiques required to find a suitable product, but that the multi-attribute utility approach is more effective at finding a suitable product.

compound critiquing can be used as a means to support real users to more efficiently find the product that they are looking for.
